conceptual assets.reasoning: The enable bit controls WDT operation and an exported enable: bus_access writes 'ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_enable_c)' on control-register writes; wdt_counter uses ctrl.enable in 'cnt_started <= ctrl.enable and (cnt_started or prsc_tick)' and resets the counter when 'ctrl.enable = '0''; reset_generator gates timeout resets with 'hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick'; and 'clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable' exports it. Corrupting ctrl.enable violates the implemented start/stop, reset gating and exported enable behavior. The value is stored in the internal record field ctrl.enable.

The lock bit enforces write-protection of the control register: bus_access tests 'if (ctrl.lock = '0') then' to allow storing control fields and otherwise executes 'reset_force <= '1''. The process sets the lock via 'ctrl.lock <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_lock_c) and ctrl.enable'. Integrity of ctrl.lock is required to enforce the implemented write-protection. The value is stored in ctrl.lock.

The strict bit selects whether access faults cause a hardware reset: bus_access stores 'ctrl.strict <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_strict_c)'; reset_generator computes 'hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force'. Integrity of ctrl.strict is required so that reset_force only yields hw reset when the stored strict bit indicates so. The value is stored in ctrl.strict.

The timeout field sets the expiration value used to trigger a timeout reset: bus_access assigns 'ctrl.timeout <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_timeout_msb_c downto ctrl_timeout_lsb_c)'; the RTL computes 'cnt_timeout <= '1' when (cnt_started = '1') and (cnt = ctrl.timeout) else '0'' and reset generation uses that to assert hw_rst_timeout. Corruption of ctrl.timeout changes when the implemented timeout occurs. The value is stored in ctrl.timeout.

The internal counter implements the elapsed-time state used to detect timeout: wdt_counter increments 'cnt' via 'cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1)' when 'cnt_inc = prsc_tick and cnt_started'; it is cleared when 'ctrl.enable = '0'' or 'reset_wdt = '1''. The equality 'cnt = ctrl.timeout' drives cnt_timeout and thus timeout resets, so integrity of cnt is required for correct timeout detection.

A bus write with the correct password sets reset_wdt and clears the counter: bus_access sets 'reset_wdt <= '1'' when 'bus_req_i.rw = '1'' and 'bus_req_i.addr(2) = '1'' and 'bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c'; wdt_counter then resets 'cnt' when 'reset_wdt = '1''. Integrity of reset_wdt is required because it permits software to prevent a timeout by resetting the counter.

The RTL asserts reset_force on unauthorized writes and uses it to drive access-induced resets: bus_access sets 'reset_force <= '1'' when writes occur while locked or when the supplied password is wrong; reset_generator uses it in 'hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force'. Integrity of reset_force is required because it contributes to the implemented hw reset decision.

The module's external reset is produced as 'rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access)'. The RTL computes 'hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick' (timeout path) and 'hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force' (access-fault path). Integrity of the reset output is required because these computed decisions directly determine the asserted reset delivered from the entity.

The RTL records which reset occurred and returns that field on bus reads: reset_identifier sets 'reset_cause <= "00"' on external reset, else on rising edge sets '"01"' if 'rstn_dbg_i = '0'', '"10"' if 'hw_rst_timeout = '1'', or '"11"' if 'hw_rst_access = '1''; bus_access reads this value into the response data. Integrity of reset_cause is required for correct reporting of the implemented reset reason.
